title: Condo Move-In Condition Checklist Form
subtitle: Operational move-in condition intake, evidence, qualified review, exception routing, handoff, and accountable closeout.
description: An original fillable condo move-in condition workflow that keeps identity, property-specific observations, evidence, authorization, exceptions, communication, and closeout in one traceable record.
use_case: Use when authorized property staff need to manage a condo move-in condition from intake through verified handoff without using the record to make legal, accommodation, screening, compliance, or professional conclusions.

blocks.label: Move-In Condition reference
blocks.guidance: Use one identifier across messages, evidence, work orders, and handoffs.

blocks.label: Property and location
blocks.guidance: Confirm the exact property record before collecting workflow details.

blocks.label: Reporting and routing contact
blocks.guidance: Record only contact information needed to route and update this record.

blocks.label: Agreement and possession context
blocks.guidance: Do not copy unnecessary financial, identity, or protected information.

sections.title: Inspection method, access, and evidence controls

blocks.label: Condition recording guide
blocks.guidance: Use plain observable descriptions and locally defined condition codes. Identify not-inspected, obstructed, unavailable, and not-applicable items. This baseline does not assign fault, responsibility, charges, code status, or legal effect.

blocks.label: Baseline preparation
blocks.guidance: A basic walkthrough does not replace qualified inspection or required disclosure.
items: Correct property, location, assignment, and participant identities confirmed
Inspection date, time, utility status, and lighting conditions recorded
Prior baseline or turnover record is linked when available
Evidence device date and time are checked
Personal papers, faces, credentials, and unrelated belongings are excluded
Operational communication or access support is recorded without diagnosis
Unavailable or unsafe areas are identified before inspection
Resident comments can be attached without altering original observations

blocks.label: Evidence series and limitations
blocks.guidance: Use stable references so later corrections remain traceable.

blocks.label: Uninspected areas, obstruction, access limit, or evidence exception
blocks.guidance: An omitted area must remain visible as an open item.

fields.label: Area, reason, immediate action, owner, due point, and follow-up method

blocks.label: Operational and qualified-review boundary
blocks.guidance: This move-in condition record captures operational facts, routing, evidence, and authorized handoffs. It does not determine legal rights, tenancy, responsibility, habitability, code or accessibility compliance, accommodation eligibility, screening eligibility, or a professional opinion. Authorized property staff must review applicable policy, notice, privacy, retention, fair-housing, safety, insurance, and licensed-trade requirements.

sections.title: Room, finish, fixture, and system observations
sections.guidance: Tie condition to an exact location.

blocks.label: Area-by-area condition baseline
blocks.guidance: Include entries, floors, walls, ceilings, doors, windows, storage, and supplied finishes as applicable.

blocks.label: Appliance, utility, and equipment baseline
blocks.guidance: Record only basic observable function within the participant's authority.

blocks.label: Basic visible condition observations
blocks.guidance: Presence or basic operation does not prove inspection, testing, or compliance.
items: Entry door and basic locking function observed
Visible trip, fall, sharp-edge, or broken-glass concern recorded
Visible water, moisture, sanitation, or pest concern recorded
Basic lighting and supplied-device function observed where authorized
Smoke, carbon-monoxide, sprinkler, or call devices noted without certifying them
Heating, cooling, ventilation, and plumbing concerns routed
Accessibility or communication concern routed without a compliance conclusion
Urgent condition has an immediate-control owner

blocks.label: Additional marks, cleanliness, odor, repair history, and resident comments
blocks.guidance: Avoid fault, wear, charge, or legal conclusions.

fields.label: Observable facts, source, evidence, requested correction, and unresolved disagreement

sections.title: Condo context and responsibility
sections.guidance: Apply controls that are specific to this property type.

blocks.label: Condo workflow controls
blocks.guidance: Check only controls actually reviewed; explain exceptions in the routing note.
items: Unit baseline is separated from hallway and common-element condition
Elevator reservation, loading path, and move protection are recorded
Lobby, corridor, door, and wall evidence identifies exact location
Fob, parking, storage, mailbox, and amenity credentials are reconciled
Association move rules are referenced without interpreting them
Owner and tenant handover responsibilities are separately assigned
Common-area damage concern is routed before a responsibility decision
Building management receives the completed access-item register

blocks.label: Responsibility and external handoff
blocks.guidance: A routing field records ownership; it does not decide disputed responsibility.

blocks.label: Condo coordination facts and unresolved questions
blocks.guidance: Separate observed facts from assumptions and identify the next authorized reviewer.

fields.label: Property-specific facts, limitations, handoff details, and unresolved question

sections.title: Access items, inventory, and correction register
sections.guidance: Reconcile handover items and open work.

blocks.label: Keys, credentials, remotes, parking, and supplied items
blocks.guidance: Do not record passwords, PINs, or full credential values.

blocks.label: Pre-occupancy correction and follow-up register
blocks.guidance: Keep disputed or deferred items open until their disposition is recorded.

blocks.label: Correction review status
blocks.guidance: Counts are operational summaries and do not determine responsibility.

sections.title: Resident comments, handover, and closeout
sections.guidance: Close only after baseline and open items are handed off.

blocks.label: Resident additions, corrections, disagreement, or later evidence
blocks.guidance: Preserve the resident's account and the original observation as separate records.

fields.label: Resident statement, evidence reference, requested correction, response owner, and status

blocks.label: Handover verification
blocks.guidance: Acknowledgment of receipt does not waive corrections or disputes.
items: Condition baseline and evidence references are complete
Uninspected or disputed areas remain visible
Issued items and access records reconcile
Urgent conditions have immediate controls and owners
Open corrections have due points and verification methods
Resident reporting, emergency, and after-hours routes were provided
Resident received a copy or approved access to the record
Qualified review and retention routing are complete

blocks.label: Final handover status
blocks.guidance: Do not mark complete while a required inspection or handoff is missing.

blocks.label: Condition record preparation and acknowledgment
blocks.guidance: Signatures confirm participation or receipt only and do not establish agreement, fault, charges, waiver, or legal acceptance.
